topic.title: AMC moviegoers spend $7.87 each on snacks, and the food itself costs AMC a small share of it while studios take half of every ticket

title: AMC charges $12.73 a ticket. Why does it care more about your popcorn? 🍿
description:
Why would AMC, the world's biggest cinema chain, care more about your popcorn than your ticket?
Sources: AMC Entertainment (Sep 2026). The characters are not advisers.
Illustrative only. Not financial advice.

Logo: AMC Theatres, Public domain, via Wikimedia Commons (https://commons.wikimedia.org/wiki/File:AMC_Theatres_logo.svg)
cta: Popcorn or the film: which is AMC really selling? Comment

lines.text: Why does AMC want your popcorn money more than your ticket money?
Not on the ticket: 50% of every ticket dollar goes to the studio that made the film.
So AMC looks to the snack bar, where each moviegoer spends $7.87.
From July to September, AMC's snack bars took in $589.4M in all.
But the popcorn, drinks and candy themselves cost AMC very little.
So the food costs AMC just 18% of what you pay for it.
Popcorn or the film: which one is AMC really selling? Because

[scene] 17.5 s, beat office (CashOffice): the counting display's '$589.4M' is larger than its own screen; it spills over the SEPTEMBER calendar on the left and runs to within ~25 px of the right edge, into the right-hand button zone. Size the figure to fit inside the display.

Put the guard in front of or beside the cart and keep the two ticket halves apart and opaque.
